experiences.name: Northern Lights Hunt by Super Jeep
experiences.description: Join a guided super jeep tour into the Icelandic wilderness away from city light pollution for the best chance of witnessing the Aurora Borealis. Expert guides track solar activity and cloud cover in real time to maximize your viewing experience. Includes hot chocolate and photography tips.
experiences.location: Golden Circle & Þingvellir National Park, Southwest Iceland

experiences.name: Blue Lagoon Geothermal Spa
experiences.description: Soak in the world-famous milky-blue geothermal waters rich in silica and minerals. Enjoy in-water massages, silica mud masks, and a swim-up bar. Booking the evening session dramatically increases your chances of seeing the northern lights dancing above while you relax in the warm 38°C waters.

experiences.name: Secret Lagoon (Gamla Laugin) Soak
experiences.description: Experience Iceland's oldest swimming pool, a natural hot spring dating back to 1891 surrounded by geysers and steaming vents. Far less crowded than the Blue Lagoon, this authentic geothermal pool sits in a stunning rural landscape and offers a genuinely local bathing experience at a fraction of the cost.

experiences.name: Reykjavik Food & Culture Walking Tour
experiences.description: Explore Iceland's vibrant capital through its food scene and Viking heritage. Sample traditional Skyr, lamb soup (Kjötsúpa), fermented shark (Hákarl), and fresh langoustine at local markets and restaurants. Visit the iconic Hallgrímskirkja church, the colorful old harbor, and learn about Norse mythology and Icelandic sagas from a local guide.

experiences.name: Landmannalaugar Highland Hot Springs Hike
experiences.description: Trek through Iceland's dramatic multicolored rhyolite mountains in the Highlands and reward yourself with a natural geothermal hot spring soak at the end. The surreal landscape of obsidian lava fields, steaming fumaroles, and rainbow-colored mountains makes this one of Iceland's most unique and unforgettable experiences.

trip_options.title: Budget Explorer - Iceland
trip_options.description: Save money without sacrificing the experience. Perfect for travelers who value authentic local experiences over luxury.

hotel.name: Golden Circle & Þingvellir National Park, Southwest Iceland Boutique Stay
hotel.location: Golden Circle & Þingvellir National Park, Southwest Iceland

day_by_day.morning: No activities scheduled — flight arrives at 13:00
day_by_day.afternoon: Arrive at Keflavík International Airport at 13:00. Clear customs, pick up a pre-booked budget rental car (essential for Iceland travel). Purchase a local SIM card at the airport for navigation. Drive approximately 45 minutes to Reykjavík, stopping at the iconic Hallgrímskirkja church for exterior photos and a quick orientation walk around the city centre — free of charge.
day_by_day.evening: Drive onward (~1 hour) to your accommodation in the Golden Circle & Þingvellir area. Check in, unpack, and settle in. After dark, step outside and scan the sky for the Northern Lights — January is peak aurora season with long dark nights. Dress in all your layers and stay out for at least an hour.

meals.breakfast: Eat on the plane or grab a snack at the airport arrivals hall
meals.lunch: Grab a budget meal at the airport — try a hot dog (pylsa) from a kiosk (~600 ISK) or a sandwich from a convenience store
meals.dinner: Cook a simple meal at your accommodation using groceries picked up at a Bónus or Krónan supermarket on the way — pasta or soup (~1,500 ISK per person)

day_by_day.notes: Stop at a Bónus supermarket (Iceland's cheapest chain) on the way from Reykjavík to stock up on groceries for self-catering breakfasts and some dinners. This will save significant money throughout the trip. Download the Vedur app (Icelandic Met Office) for aurora and weather forecasts.

day_by_day.morning: Visit Þingvellir National Park — a UNESCO World Heritage Site and completely free to enter. Walk the Almannagjá gorge, which sits directly on the Mid-Atlantic Ridge where the North American and Eurasian tectonic plates meet. Explore the historic Alþingi parliament site and admire the Öxará River, partially frozen in January.
day_by_day.afternoon: Continue the classic Golden Circle route. Visit the famous Geysir geothermal area — the original geyser and the highly active Strokkur, which erupts every 5–10 minutes shooting boiling water 20–30 metres into the air. Completely free to walk around the geothermal field. Then drive to the majestic Gullfoss waterfall, partially frozen in winter and utterly dramatic — also free.
day_by_day.evening: Return to accommodation. Tonight is another prime Northern Lights opportunity. Check the Vedur aurora forecast app — if activity is predicted above level 3, drive to a dark spot away from any light pollution (Þingvellir lake shore is excellent). Bring a thermos of hot chocolate.

meals.breakfast: Self-catered at accommodation — oats, yogurt, skyr (Icelandic yogurt), and fruit bought at Bónus (~500 ISK)
meals.lunch: Pack sandwiches and snacks from your grocery supplies to eat at Geysir or Gullfoss — there are picnic tables and covered areas
meals.dinner: Self-catered dinner at accommodation — try making lamb soup (kjötsúpa) with a packet mix from the supermarket, a beloved Icelandic staple (~800 ISK per person)

day_by_day.notes: Þingvellir, Geysir, and Gullfoss are all free. Wear ice cleats (available cheaply at Bónus or Krónan) as paths can be extremely icy in January. Daylight hours in January are very limited — roughly 9:30am to 4:30pm — so plan outdoor sightseeing within this window.

day_by_day.morning: Drive south toward the Secret Lagoon (Gamla Laugin) in Flúðir, the oldest swimming pool in Iceland. At around 3,000–3,500 ISK entry, it is significantly cheaper than the Blue Lagoon and far more authentic. Soak in the naturally heated geothermal pool surrounded by small geysers and hot springs — a magical winter experience.
day_by_day.afternoon: Explore the charming village of Flúðir and its surrounding greenhouse farms. Drive to Kerið volcanic crater lake — entry is 700 ISK, making it one of Iceland's best-value sights. The vivid red volcanic rock contrasts beautifully with the teal-green lake below, and in January the crater rim may be dusted with snow.
day_by_day.evening: Drive back toward the Þingvellir area. Stop at a local swimming pool (sundlaug) — every Icelandic town has one with geothermally heated outdoor pools and hot pots. Entry is typically 1,000–1,200 ISK. This is how locals relax and it is an unmissable cultural experience. Watch for Northern Lights on the drive back.

meals.breakfast: Self-catered at accommodation — eggs, toast, and skyr
meals.lunch: Pick up a budget lunch at the Flúðir local store or pack your own — a filled baguette or soup (~800–1,200 ISK if buying out)
meals.dinner: Self-catered — cook rice and fish (skrei cod is in season in January and available cheaply at supermarkets) (~1,000 ISK per person)

day_by_day.notes: The Secret Lagoon is far less crowded than the Blue Lagoon, especially on weekday mornings. Book in advance online. Bring your own towel to avoid rental fees. The local swimming pools (sundlaugar) are a genuine Icelandic cultural institution — do not skip this experience.

day_by_day.morning: Take a morning drive to Hveragerði, a geothermal town famous for its hot springs and greenhouses. Walk through the town and visit the free outdoor geothermal park in the centre where hot water bubbles up from the ground. The town sits on extremely active geothermal ground — fascinating to explore.
day_by_day.afternoon: Hike the Reykjadalur Hot Spring River trail from Hveragerði. This is a free hike (approximately 3km each way) leading to a naturally heated river where you can bathe in geothermally warmed water flowing through a valley. In January the contrast of snow on the hillsides and steaming warm water is spectacular. Allow 2–3 hours total.
day_by_day.evening: Drive back to accommodation via Selfoss town for a supermarket resupply at Krónan. This evening, attend a free Northern Lights hunt — drive to the Þingvellir lakeshore or any elevated dark spot. The Vedur app will guide your timing. Stay out for 1–2 hours if aurora activity is forecast.

meals.breakfast: Self-catered — skyr with granola and coffee
meals.lunch: Pack a hot thermos of soup and sandwiches for the Reykjadalur hike — essential for warmth on a winter trail
meals.dinner: Treat yourself to a budget meal out in Selfoss — try Krónan deli section or a local grill restaurant. A burger or fish and chips runs ~2,500–3,000 ISK

day_by_day.notes: The Reykjadalur trail can be icy and challenging in January — wear proper hiking boots with crampons and dress in full waterproof layers. The hot river bathing is one of Iceland's most unique free experiences. Bring a dry bag for your clothes and a towel. The trail head is well-signed from central Hveragerði.

day_by_day.morning: Drive the stunning South Coast highway (Route 1) east toward Seljalandsfoss waterfall. Walk behind the curtain of water through the cave — a surreal experience. In January the surrounding ice formations and frozen spray create an ethereal winter landscape. Entry is free (parking fee ~750 ISK). Nearby Gljúfrabúi hidden canyon waterfall is also free and unmissable.
day_by_day.afternoon: Continue east to Skógafoss, one of Iceland's most powerful and beautiful waterfalls. Climb the 527 steps to the top for panoramic views over the South Coast and the Eyjafjallajökull glacier. Free entry. Then drive to the black sand beach at Reynisfjara near Vík — one of the world's most dramatic beaches with towering basalt columns and crashing Atlantic waves. Completely free.
day_by_day.evening: Explore the small village of Vík í Mýrdal. Visit the iconic black church (Víkurkirkja) perched on the hill above the village — free and atmospheric at dusk. Check into a budget guesthouse or hostel in Vík for the night (pre-book in advance) to allow an early start the next day. Watch for Northern Lights from the beach.

meals.breakfast: Self-catered early breakfast before departure — overnight oats prepared the night before
meals.lunch: Pack lunch from home supplies — eat at Skógafoss picnic area
meals.dinner: Vík has limited but reasonable options — try the Suður-Vík restaurant for a budget fish soup (~2,000 ISK) or pick up groceries at the N1 petrol station convenience store for a self-catered meal

day_by_day.notes: CRITICAL SAFETY WARNING: Never turn your back on the ocean at Reynisfjara — the sneaker waves here are extremely dangerous and have killed tourists. Stay well back from the water's edge. Seljalandsfoss path behind the waterfall may be closed in icy conditions — check signage on arrival. This is a long driving day (~2.5 hours one way) so depart early to maximise the limited daylight.

day_by_day.morning: Early morning drive from Vík east to Jökulsárlón Glacier Lagoon — Iceland's most iconic and dramatic landscape. Watch icebergs calving from the Breiðamerkurjökull glacier and floating silently through the lagoon. Seals often rest on the icebergs in winter. Entry to the lagoon viewing area is free. Walk along the shore for an hour.
day_by_day.afternoon: Walk 200 metres to Diamond Beach — the black sand beach where glacial ice chunks wash ashore and glitter like diamonds in the winter light. Completely free and utterly breathtaking. Spend time photographing and exploring. Then drive back west, stopping at the Fjaðrárgljúfur canyon (if road conditions permit in January) — a dramatic 100-metre deep canyon, free to visit.
day_by_day.evening: Return drive toward your Golden Circle accommodation. This is a long driving day — approximately 5 hours total driving. Stop at Kirkjubæjarklaustur for a petrol station hot dog and coffee. Arrive back at accommodation, cook a simple dinner, and check aurora forecast for a late-night sky watch.

meals.breakfast: Early self-catered breakfast at Vík accommodation or a petrol station pastry and coffee on the road (~600 ISK)
meals.lunch: Pack a substantial lunch — sandwiches, nuts, chocolate bars, and a thermos of hot soup for the glacier lagoon
meals.dinner: Self-catered at accommodation — a hearty pasta dish with canned tomato sauce and vegetables (~800 ISK per person)

day_by_day.notes: Jökulsárlón is approximately 380km from Reykjavík — this is the furthest point of the trip and requires an early start. Check road conditions on road.is before departing (F-roads will be closed but Route 1 is generally maintained). January light at the glacier lagoon is magical — the blue ice glows even in low light. Fill up petrol whenever you see a station on the South Coast as they are sparse.

day_by_day.morning: Rest and recovery day after yesterday's long drive. Sleep in and enjoy a leisurely self-catered breakfast. Visit the geothermal swimming pool at Laugarvatn Fontana — a wonderful mid-range hot spring spa on the shores of Lake Laugarvatn, just 10 minutes from Þingvellir. Entry ~3,500 ISK but includes access to steam rooms built directly over natural geothermal vents in the ground.
day_by_day.afternoon: Explore Laugarvatn village and walk along the frozen lake shore. Visit the Lindin restaurant area for a warm drink. Drive to the Faxi waterfall (Vatnsleysufoss) — a wide, low waterfall on the Hvítá river that is much less visited than Gullfoss and completely free. Beautiful in winter light.
day_by_day.evening: Return to accommodation for a relaxed evening. Cook a special dinner using Icelandic lamb from the supermarket — Iceland produces world-class free-range lamb. Check aurora forecast and if conditions are good (clear skies, KP index 3+), drive to Þingvellir lake for a dedicated Northern Lights photography session.

meals.breakfast: Leisurely self-catered breakfast — pancakes or French toast with Icelandic butter and jam
meals.lunch: Light lunch at Laugarvatn — try the geothermal rye bread (hverabrauð) baked underground, sold at Fontana (~1,500 ISK for a tasting)
meals.dinner: Self-catered Icelandic lamb chops with roasted root vegetables — a true taste of Iceland (~2,000 ISK per person for quality lamb from Bónus)

day_by_day.notes: Laugarvatn Fontana is a more affordable and authentic alternative to the Blue Lagoon. The geothermal rye bread baked underground in a pot is a unique Icelandic tradition — try it here. Today is intentionally slower-paced to rest legs and recharge for the remaining week.

day_by_day.morning: Drive north from Þingvellir toward the Snæfellsnes Peninsula (approximately 2.5 hours). This dramatic peninsula inspired Jules Verne's 'Journey to the Centre of the Earth.' Stop at Borgarnes Settlement Centre for a coffee and a brief look at the Viking history exhibition exterior — the building itself is architecturally interesting from outside.
day_by_day.afternoon: Explore Snæfellsjökull National Park — the glacier-capped volcano at the tip of the peninsula. Visit Djúpalónssandur black pebble beach with its dramatic lava rock formations and old shipwreck remains — free. Walk the coastal path to Dritvík cove. Then visit Arnarstapi village with its stunning basalt arch sea cliffs and Arctic tern colonies (inactive in winter but the rock formations remain dramatic).
day_by_day.evening: Check into a budget guesthouse or hostel in Grundarfjörður or Stykkishólmur for the night. The iconic Kirkjufell mountain ('Arrow Head Mountain' from Game of Thrones) is right in Grundarfjörður — walk to the waterfall viewpoint at dusk and stay for Northern Lights photography. Kirkjufell with aurora overhead is one of Iceland's most photographed scenes.

meals.breakfast: Self-catered early breakfast before the long drive
meals.lunch: Pack sandwiches and eat with views of Snæfellsjökull glacier — picnic at Djúpalónssandur beach
meals.dinner: Grundarfjörður has a small grocery store — self-cater a warming fish stew or buy a pizza from the local petrol station (~1,500 ISK)

day_by_day.notes: Kirkjufell and Northern Lights is one of the most iconic photo opportunities in Iceland — arrive at the waterfall viewpoint (Kirkjufellsfoss) before dark to set up. The Snæfellsnes Peninsula is often called 'Iceland in miniature' as it contains glaciers, lava fields, fishing villages, beaches, and mountains in a compact area. Pre-book accommodation well in advance as options are limited.

day_by_day.morning: Early morning Kirkjufell sunrise attempt (around 10:30am in January). Then drive around the north side of the Snæfellsnes Peninsula through Ólafsvík and Rif to Stykkishólmur — a charming fishing town with colourful houses and a distinctive lighthouse on a rocky island. Walk the harbour area and climb to the lighthouse viewpoint for free panoramic views.
day_by_day.afternoon: Drive the south side of the peninsula back east. Stop at Búðir black church — one of Iceland's most photographed buildings, a tiny isolated black wooden church against the backdrop of the glacier and lava field. Free to visit and photograph. Continue to Ytri Tunga beach — one of the best places in Iceland to spot wild Atlantic seals year-round, completely free.
day_by_day.evening: Drive back toward the Golden Circle accommodation (approximately 2 hours). Stop in Borgarnes for a supermarket resupply. This evening, if aurora forecast is favourable, head to Þingvellir lake for sky watching. Alternatively, enjoy a relaxed evening at accommodation and plan the remaining days.

meals.breakfast: Guesthouse breakfast if included, or self-catered at accommodation
meals.lunch: Stop at the Narfeyrarstofa restaurant in Stykkishólmur for their famous seafood soup — a splurge at ~2,500 ISK but worth it for fresh local langoustine
meals.dinner: Self-catered at Golden Circle accommodation — soup and bread from supermarket supplies

day_by_day.notes: The seals at Ytri Tunga are almost always present and completely wild — approach quietly and stay on the beach path. The Búðir black church is most atmospheric in low winter light or snowfall. The drive back from Snæfellsnes along Route 54 and Route 1 is straightforward but allow extra time for icy road conditions.

day_by_day.morning: Day trip north to the Reykjanes Peninsula — Iceland's most geologically active area. Visit the Bridge Between Continents at Sandvík — a small footbridge spanning the crack between the North American and Eurasian tectonic plates. Free to visit (small fee for a certificate if desired). Walk the surrounding lava field and fissure zone.
day_by_day.afternoon: Explore the Reykjanes UNESCO Global Geopark. Visit Gunnuhver hot spring — Iceland's largest mud pool, dramatically steaming and bubbling with boiling sulphurous mud. Free to visit. Walk the surrounding geothermal landscape on boardwalks. Then visit the Reykjanesviti lighthouse — Iceland's oldest lighthouse — with views of dramatic coastal cliffs and crashing waves.
day_by_day.evening: Drive to Grindavík for a look at the fishing harbour town and pick up fresh fish directly from the harbour fish shop at very reasonable prices. Return to accommodation. Tonight, do a final major Northern Lights hunt — check the Vedur forecast and if KP index is 3 or above with clear skies, drive to a completely dark location. The Þingvellir lakeshore or the Reykjanes lava fields are excellent.

meals.breakfast: Self-catered at accommodation
meals.lunch: Pack lunch from home supplies for the Reykjanes Peninsula exploration
meals.dinner: Cook fresh fish purchased from Grindavík harbour — pan-fried cod or haddock with potatoes (~1,200 ISK per person for very fresh fish)

day_by_day.notes: The Reykjanes Peninsula has seen significant volcanic activity in recent years (eruptions in 2021–2024). Check current volcanic activity status at vedur.is before visiting. The area may have restricted access zones — always follow official guidance. Gunnuhver hot spring is extremely hot and dangerous — stay strictly on the boardwalks.

day_by_day.morning: Visit Reykjavík for a full day. Start with a walk up to Hallgrímskirkja church — take the lift to the tower for panoramic city views (~1,000 ISK). Walk down Skólavörðustígur street to the old harbour. Visit the Sun Voyager sculpture (Sólfar) on the waterfront — free and iconic.
day_by_day.afternoon: Explore the Reykjavík old town (Tjörnin lake, the parliament building Alþingishúsið, the old cemetery). Visit the National Museum of Iceland (~2,000 ISK) for an excellent overview of Icelandic history and culture — well worth the entry fee. Walk Laugavegur shopping street for window shopping and people-watching.
day_by_day.evening: Experience Reykjavík's famous hot pot culture at Sundhöllin or Vesturbæjarlaug swimming pool (~1,000 ISK entry). Soak in the outdoor hot pots with locals as darkness falls — this is quintessential Reykjavík. For dinner, explore the budget food options on Laugavegur before driving back to accommodation.

meals.breakfast: Self-catered early breakfast before driving to Reykjavík
meals.lunch: Reykjavík's cheapest and most iconic meal: a hot dog (pylsa) from Bæjarins Beztu Pylsur — the famous hot dog stand near the harbour (~500 ISK). Get it 'with everything' (með öllu)
meals.dinner: Reykjavík budget dining — try Hlöllabátar for a budget sandwich (~1,800 ISK) or Noodle Station for Asian noodle soup (~2,000 ISK), one of the city's best budget restaurants

day_by_day.notes: Bæjarins Beztu Pylsur hot dogs are a genuine Reykjavík institution — Bill Clinton famously ate one here. The Icelandic hot dog uses lamb meat and is topped with raw and crispy fried onions, ketchup, mustard, and remoulade. The National Museum is one of the best value museums in Iceland. Reykjavík parking can be expensive — use the P4 or P5 car parks near the city centre.

day_by_day.morning: Return to Þingvellir National Park for a deeper exploration — the park is enormous and there are several trails not covered on Day 2. Walk the Lögberg (Law Rock) area and explore the Öxará River gorge. In January the river may be partially frozen, creating beautiful ice formations. The park is free to enter.
day_by_day.afternoon: Drive to Nesjavellir geothermal power plant — one of the largest geothermal energy facilities in the world, visible from the road with massive steam plumes rising against the winter sky. The exterior and surrounding landscape are free to view and photograph. Continue to Lake Þingvallavatn — Iceland's largest natural lake — for a scenic lakeside walk.
day_by_day.evening: Final dedicated Northern Lights evening. This is your last full night in Iceland with dark skies. Set an alarm for midnight and check the Vedur aurora forecast obsessively throughout the day. If KP index reaches 4–5, drive to the Þingvellir lake shore or a high elevated road with clear northern horizon. Bring all your warmest clothes, a tripod if you have one, and hot drinks.

meals.breakfast: Special self-catered breakfast — make skyr pancakes (skyrpönnukökur) using skyr, flour, and eggs — a traditional Icelandic treat
meals.lunch: Pack a warm lunch for Þingvellir — thermos soup and rye bread with smoked salmon (a classic Icelandic open sandwich)
meals.dinner: Celebratory final dinner — cook Icelandic lamb with roasted vegetables and skyr-based sauce at accommodation (~2,500 ISK for a quality meal)

day_by_day.notes: This is statistically your best remaining chance for Northern Lights. January in Iceland has some of the highest aurora activity of the year. The key factors are: clear skies (check cloud forecast on vedur.is), solar activity (check spaceweather.com), and dark location. Even a KP index of 2–3 can produce visible aurora from a truly dark location. Do not give up — some of the best displays happen after midnight.

day_by_day.morning: Final morning in Iceland. Pack up accommodation and check out. Drive toward Keflavík Airport (approximately 1–1.5 hours from the Golden Circle area). Stop at the Blue Lagoon road for exterior photos — you can see the famous milky blue water from the road without paying the expensive entry fee. Stop in Hafnarfjörður town for a final Icelandic coffee and pastry.
day_by_day.afternoon: Arrive at Keflavík Airport with plenty of time. Return rental car (allow 30–45 minutes for this process). Check in and go through security. Browse the duty-free shop — Icelandic spirits (Brennivín schnapps), Icelandic chocolate, and skyr are good budget souvenirs. The duty-free shop is often cheaper than in-town prices for alcohol.
day_by_day.evening: Depart Iceland. Reflect on 13 extraordinary days of glaciers, geysers, hot springs, and (hopefully) Northern Lights dancing overhead.

meals.breakfast: Final self-catered breakfast using remaining food supplies — clear out the fridge creatively
meals.lunch: Airport meal — Keflavík Airport has a 10-11 café and a Pylsuvagninn hot dog stand which are the most budget-friendly options (~1,500–2,000 ISK)
meals.dinner: In-flight meal or airport dining

day_by_day.notes: Return the rental car with a full tank of petrol — filling up at the airport petrol station is slightly more expensive than at a Bónus or Orkan station in a nearby town. Allow extra time for car return as queues can form. Keflavík Airport is approximately 50km from Reykjavík and 80km from the Golden Circle — factor in potential winter road delays. Iceland requires you to pay outstanding road tolls (Hvalfjarðargöng tunnel if used) before departure. Final budget tip: the total trip cost for self-catering most meals, using a budget rental car, and staying in budget accommodation should come to approximately 150,000–200,000 ISK (~€1,000–€1,400) per person excluding flights.

trip_options.title: Classic Iceland Experience
trip_options.description: The sweet spot between comfort and value. Enjoy quality accommodations, diverse experiences, and good food.

hotel.name: Golden Circle & Þingvellir National Park, Southwest Iceland Boutique Stay
hotel.location: Golden Circle & Þingvellir National Park, Southwest Iceland

experiences.name: Blue Lagoon Geothermal Spa
experiences.description: Soak in the world-famous milky-blue geothermal waters rich in silica and minerals. Enjoy in-water massages, silica mud masks, and a swim-up bar. Booking the evening session dramatically increases your chances of seeing the northern lights dancing above while you relax in the warm 38°C waters.

day_by_day.morning: Flight arrives at Keflavík International Airport at 13:00 — no morning activities scheduled. Clear customs, collect luggage, and pick up pre-booked rental car (4WD recommended for January conditions).
day_by_day.afternoon: Drive from Keflavík to the Blue Lagoon Geothermal Spa (only 20 minutes away — perfect first stop before heading to your hotel). Pre-booked entry essential. Soak in the iconic milky-blue silica-rich waters, enjoy the in-water mineral mask bar, and decompress after the flight. Spend 2–3 hours here.
day_by_day.evening: Continue the 1.5-hour drive to your boutique accommodation in the Golden Circle & Þingvellir area. Check in, settle in, and enjoy a relaxed dinner at or near the hotel. If the sky clears, step outside after dinner for a first northern lights watch — January offers up to 18 hours of darkness.

meals.breakfast: On the flight or grab a snack at Keflavík Airport arrivals hall (Dunkin' or airport café)
meals.lunch: Blue Lagoon Lava Restaurant or MOSS Restaurant on-site (mid-range set menu, budget ~4,000–6,000 ISK)
meals.dinner: Hotel restaurant or nearby Lindin Restaurant in Laugarvatn village — known for warm Icelandic comfort food and local fish dishes (~4,500–6,500 ISK)

day_by_day.notes: Book Blue Lagoon tickets well in advance — January slots sell out. Roads between Keflavík and the Golden Circle are generally well-maintained but check road.is before driving. Dress in warm layers for the outdoor drive and evening aurora watch.

day_by_day.morning: Visit Þingvellir National Park — a UNESCO World Heritage Site and the rift valley where the North American and Eurasian tectonic plates meet. Walk the Almannagjá gorge trail (short, well-marked, about 1.5–2 hours). The dramatic winter light over the frozen landscape is extraordinary.
day_by_day.afternoon: Drive to the Geysir Geothermal Area (about 45 minutes from Þingvellir). Watch Strokkur geyser erupt every 5–10 minutes shooting water 20–30 meters into the air. Explore the surrounding hot spring field. Then continue to Gullfoss Waterfall (15 minutes away) — Iceland's most iconic double-tiered waterfall, especially dramatic with winter ice formations.
day_by_day.evening: Return to your hotel. After dinner, join a guided northern lights tour departing from the Golden Circle area (many local operators offer evening jeep tours with expert aurora guides who chase clear skies — approximately 9,000–12,000 ISK per person).

meals.breakfast: Hotel breakfast buffet (included or ~2,000–2,500 ISK) — fuel up for a full day outdoors
meals.lunch: Geysir Center café or Gullfoss Café near the waterfall — hearty soup, bread, and coffee (~2,500–3,500 ISK)
meals.dinner: Friðheimar Greenhouse Restaurant near Reykholt — unique dining inside a geothermal tomato greenhouse, famous for tomato soup and fresh produce (~5,000–7,000 ISK, reservation required)

day_by_day.notes: Þingvellir paths can be icy in January — wear crampons or ice cleats (available cheaply at Reykjavík outdoor stores or some hotels). Check aurora forecast on vedur.is or the Icelandic Met Office app each evening.

day_by_day.morning: Visit the Fontana Geothermal Baths in Laugarvatn village (5 minutes from many Golden Circle accommodations). Soak in naturally heated pools fed by geothermal springs directly on the lake shore. A more intimate, local alternative to the Blue Lagoon. Enjoy the traditional rye bread baked underground in the geothermal soil.
day_by_day.afternoon: Drive to Kerið Volcanic Crater (about 30 minutes south). Walk the rim of this 6,500-year-old red and black volcanic crater with a vivid teal lake at the bottom — stunning in winter light. Then explore the Skálholt Cathedral, one of Iceland's most historically significant religious sites, just a short detour away.
day_by_day.evening: Return to the hotel for a quiet evening. Set an alarm for midnight and check the aurora forecast — if KP index is 3+ and skies are clear, head outside or drive a few minutes from any light pollution for a potential aurora display. Keep a thermos of hot chocolate ready.

meals.breakfast: Hotel breakfast or self-catered — pick up supplies at a Krónan or Bónus supermarket for budget-friendly morning meals
meals.lunch: Laugarvatn Fontana café on-site — fresh bread, soup, and geothermal-baked rye bread tasting (~2,000–3,000 ISK)
meals.dinner: Hotel restaurant or self-catered hot meal at accommodation — January is a great time to try Icelandic lamb stew (kjötsúpa) from a supermarket kit (~1,500–2,500 ISK)

day_by_day.notes: Fontana Geothermal Baths entry is approximately 3,500–4,500 ISK. Kerið crater has a small entrance fee (~700 ISK). January days are very short (sunrise ~11:00, sunset ~16:00) — plan outdoor sightseeing between 10:00 and 16:00 to maximize daylight.

day_by_day.morning: Take a morning drive to Haukadalur Valley area and explore lesser-visited hot springs and mud pools away from the main Geysir crowds. Enjoy the surreal steaming landscape in the cold morning air. Photography is exceptional in the low winter light.
day_by_day.afternoon: Drive toward the Langjökull glacier area (about 1 hour from the Golden Circle). Book a snowmobile tour or glacier snowcat excursion on Langjökull — Iceland's second-largest glacier. Several operators run afternoon tours from the base camp. This is a bucket-list winter experience (~20,000–28,000 ISK per person).
day_by_day.evening: Return to the hotel. Warm up with a hot shower and a long dinner. Check aurora forecast and do a dedicated 30-minute aurora watch from the hotel grounds or a nearby dark spot before bed.

meals.breakfast: Hotel breakfast — eat well before the glacier excursion
meals.lunch: Pack a lunch from the hotel or grab snacks from a petrol station — glacier tours often don't include food stops
meals.dinner: Hótel Gullfoss restaurant or Bjarteyjarsandur farmhouse restaurant (if open) — Icelandic lamb, fish of the day, and skyr dessert (~5,500–7,500 ISK)

day_by_day.notes: Glacier tours require booking in advance. Dress in extreme warmth — glacier wind chill can be severe. Operators typically provide outer suits but bring thermal underlayers, gloves, and a balaclava. Confirm road and weather conditions the morning of the excursion.

day_by_day.morning: Explore the Nesjavellir Geothermal Power Plant (about 20 minutes from Þingvellir) — a fascinating look at how Iceland harnesses volcanic energy to heat homes and generate electricity. The steaming pipes and industrial landscape against snow-capped mountains are visually striking. Free or low-cost entry.
day_by_day.afternoon: Drive to Lake Þingvallavatn — Iceland's largest natural lake — and walk the shoreline trails near Þingvellir. In winter, the lake may be partially frozen with incredible ice formations. The area is also known for snorkeling/diving in Silfra fissure (crystal-clear glacial water between tectonic plates) — book a dry suit snorkel tour if interested (~18,000–22,000 ISK).
day_by_day.evening: Aurora hunting evening. Drive to a pre-scouted dark location away from any settlement lights (the Þingvellir area is excellent for this). Bring a tripod for long-exposure aurora photography. Spend 1–2 hours watching the sky before returning to the hotel.

meals.breakfast: Hotel breakfast
meals.lunch: Þingvellir National Park visitor center café — hot soup and sandwiches (~2,000–3,000 ISK)
meals.dinner: Apotek Kitchen + Bar in nearby Selfoss town (30-minute drive) — modern Icelandic cuisine in a relaxed setting (~5,000–7,000 ISK)

day_by_day.notes: Silfra snorkeling requires advance booking and is cold even in dry suits — water temperature is 2–4°C year-round. The Nesjavellir road may be restricted in severe weather — check road.is. Carry a fully charged power bank and hand warmers for the aurora watch.

day_by_day.morning: Visit the Secret Lagoon (Gamla Laugin) in Flúðir village — one of Iceland's oldest swimming pools, fed by natural hot springs. Much less crowded than the Blue Lagoon, more authentic, and surrounded by geothermal activity including a small geyser that erupts every few minutes. Soak for 2 hours (~3,000–3,500 ISK entry).
day_by_day.afternoon: Explore the Hrunalaug Hot Spring — a small, naturally occurring hot spring pool near Flúðir (free, but respect the site and leave no trace). Then visit the nearby Bruarfoss Waterfall, known for its vivid blue water — a 45-minute round-trip hike through snowy terrain.
day_by_day.evening: Relaxed evening at the hotel. Enjoy the hotel's common areas, perhaps a sauna or hot tub if available. Light dinner and early night to be well-rested for the coming days.

meals.breakfast: Self-catered or hotel breakfast
meals.lunch: Flúðir village — Minilik Restaurant (Ethiopian-Icelandic fusion, surprisingly excellent) or the local petrol station grill (~2,000–3,500 ISK)
meals.dinner: Hotel restaurant — try the Icelandic fish soup (plokkfiskur) and fresh bread (~4,000–5,500 ISK)

day_by_day.notes: Hrunalaug is on private farmland — a small donation box is present and etiquette requires quiet, respectful use. Bruarfoss trail can be icy; use ice cleats. The Secret Lagoon is a highlight of the Golden Circle area and highly recommended for hot spring enthusiasts.

day_by_day.morning: Day trip toward South Iceland — drive the Ring Road east toward Seljalandsfoss Waterfall (about 1.5 hours from the Golden Circle). Walk behind the waterfall (the path may be icy/closed in January — check conditions). The frozen spray and icicles make this a winter wonderland scene.
day_by_day.afternoon: Continue to Skógafoss Waterfall (15 minutes east of Seljalandsfoss) — one of Iceland's largest and most dramatic waterfalls. Climb the 370 steps to the viewing platform for panoramic views. Then visit the nearby Skógar Folk Museum for a glimpse into traditional Icelandic rural life.
day_by_day.evening: Drive back toward the Golden Circle. Stop at a petrol station for a classic Icelandic hot dog (pylsur) — a beloved local tradition. Arrive at hotel, warm up, and do an aurora watch before bed.

meals.breakfast: Hotel breakfast — early start needed for the day trip
meals.lunch: Skógafoss café or food truck near the waterfall (~2,500–3,500 ISK) — hot soup and waffles
meals.dinner: Hotel restaurant or self-catered — pick up fresh fish from a supermarket and cook if your accommodation has kitchen facilities (~1,500–2,500 ISK)

day_by_day.notes: The path behind Seljalandsfoss is sometimes closed in winter due to ice — check locally before attempting. Dress in full waterproof gear as the mist from the waterfalls soaks everything. This is a long driving day (~3–4 hours total) — start by 9:00 to maximize the limited daylight.

day_by_day.morning: Rest and recovery morning — sleep in, enjoy a leisurely hotel breakfast, and browse local handicraft shops or the hotel's book collection. January can bring unpredictable storms — use this as a flexible buffer day.
day_by_day.afternoon: Visit the Laugarvatn village area for a self-guided walk along the lake shore. Stop at local art galleries or craft shops in the village. Alternatively, if weather is good, revisit Þingvellir for a longer hike along the Öxará River trail.
day_by_day.evening: Dedicated northern lights evening. Book a guided aurora tour with a local operator who monitors forecasts in real time and drives guests to optimal viewing locations. Many tours include hot chocolate and aurora photography tips. (~9,000–14,000 ISK per person).

meals.breakfast: Long, relaxed hotel breakfast
meals.lunch: Laugarvatn village café — waffles with jam and cream, a beloved Icelandic tradition (~1,500–2,000 ISK)
meals.dinner: Lindin Restaurant in Laugarvatn — upscale-casual Icelandic dining, Arctic char, lamb, and local vegetables (~5,500–8,000 ISK)

day_by_day.notes: Day 8 is intentionally lighter to allow for rest, weather flexibility, and a dedicated aurora experience in the evening. Aurora tours are most successful when you trust a local guide who monitors real-time satellite cloud cover maps — worth the investment.

day_by_day.morning: Drive to Reykjavik (about 45–60 minutes from the Golden Circle). Explore the city's highlights: Hallgrímskirkja Church (take the elevator to the tower for panoramic views), Harpa Concert Hall, and the Old Harbour area.
day_by_day.afternoon: Visit the National Museum of Iceland for a deep dive into Icelandic history and Viking heritage (~2,000 ISK entry). Then stroll Laugavegur, Reykjavik's main shopping street — browse local wool sweaters (lopapeysa), design shops, and Icelandic chocolate.
day_by_day.evening: Enjoy Reykjavik's vibrant food scene for dinner. Return to the Golden Circle hotel afterward, or if you prefer, consider booking one night in Reykjavik to fully enjoy the city (optional deviation from the main accommodation plan).

meals.breakfast: Hotel breakfast before driving to Reykjavik
meals.lunch: Reykjavik Roasters coffee shop + a nearby bakery — skyr parfait, cinnamon bun (snúður), and specialty coffee (~1,500–2,500 ISK)
meals.dinner: Grillmarkaðurinn (The Grill Market) — mid-to-upscale Icelandic grill restaurant featuring local lamb, fish, and game (~7,000–10,000 ISK) or Sægreifinn (The Sea Baron) for budget-friendly lobster soup (~2,500 ISK)

day_by_day.notes: Parking in Reykjavik requires a parking disc or paid parking app. The city is very walkable once parked centrally near Hallgrímskirkja. Budget extra time for shopping — Icelandic wool products make excellent souvenirs and are widely available in the city.

day_by_day.morning: Drive to the Reykjanes Peninsula (about 45 minutes from the Golden Circle via Reykjavik). Explore the dramatic volcanic landscape of the Reykjanes UNESCO Global Geopark — lava fields, steaming fumaroles, and dramatic coastal cliffs. Visit the Bridge Between Continents — a symbolic footbridge spanning the Mid-Atlantic Ridge.
day_by_day.afternoon: Visit the Gunnuhver Hot Springs — Iceland's largest hot spring, with powerful boiling mud pools and steam vents. Then explore Reykjanesviti Lighthouse, Iceland's oldest lighthouse, perched on dramatic coastal cliffs with views of crashing North Atlantic waves.
day_by_day.evening: Drive back to the Golden Circle hotel. This evening, set up for a long aurora watch session — the Reykjanes area has minimal light pollution in many spots, or watch from the hotel grounds. Keep your camera set up on a tripod near your room window.

meals.breakfast: Hotel breakfast
meals.lunch: Café Duus in Keflavík town — fresh fish and chips, seafood soup in a cozy harbour-side setting (~3,000–4,500 ISK)
meals.dinner: Hotel restaurant or self-catered — a good night to try Icelandic skyr with berries and granola as a lighter meal (~1,000–1,500 ISK)

day_by_day.notes: The Reykjanes Peninsula has been volcanically active since 2021 — check for any restricted zones before visiting. Gunnuhver is safe to visit from designated viewing platforms but stay on marked paths as the ground is dangerously hot. The area is very windy — dress accordingly.

day_by_day.morning: Return to Þingvellir National Park for a final, deeper exploration. Walk the full Almannagjá gorge to the Law Rock (Lögberg) — the site of Iceland's ancient parliament (Alþingi), established in 930 AD. The rift valley walls are spectacular in winter morning light.
day_by_day.afternoon: Visit Öxarárfoss Waterfall within Þingvellir — a small but beautiful waterfall that often freezes partially in January, creating stunning ice formations. Then drive to Hveragerði village (30 minutes south) — a geothermal town where you can walk the Reykjadalur Hot River Trail (about 3km each way) to a naturally heated river where you can bathe outdoors.
day_by_day.evening: Relaxed final full-day evening. Enjoy a celebratory dinner at a nice local restaurant. Do one last dedicated aurora watch from a dark spot near the hotel — January 25th may offer excellent aurora conditions depending on solar activity.

meals.breakfast: Hotel breakfast
meals.lunch: Ölverk Pizza & Brewery in Hveragerði — craft beer and wood-fired pizza in a geothermally heated building (~3,500–5,000 ISK)
meals.dinner: Friðheimar Greenhouse Restaurant (revisit or first visit) or Lindin Restaurant — a special celebratory Icelandic meal (~6,000–9,000 ISK)

day_by_day.notes: Reykjadalur Hot River Trail requires a 45–60 minute hike each way in snow — bring a dry bag for your towel and change of clothes, ice cleats, and a headlamp as it will be dark by the time you return. The hot river experience is magical and highly recommended for hot spring enthusiasts.

day_by_day.morning: Final morning in Iceland — pack, check out of the hotel, and do a slow scenic drive back toward Reykjavik and Keflavík. Stop at any final viewpoints or spots you want to revisit.
day_by_day.afternoon: Arrive in Reykjavik for last-minute shopping on Laugavegur. Pick up Icelandic souvenirs: lopapeysa wool sweaters, volcanic salt, skyr, licorice, and local gin. Visit the Kolaportið Flea Market (open Saturdays and Sundays only — if your schedule aligns) for local crafts and vintage finds.
day_by_day.evening: Final dinner in Reykjavik before heading to the airport hotel or making your way toward Keflavík for an early departure. Enjoy a memorable last Icelandic meal.

meals.breakfast: Hotel breakfast or a final Icelandic breakfast at a Reykjavik café — skyr bowl, rye bread with smoked salmon
meals.lunch: Bæjarins Beztu Pylsur — Reykjavik's most famous hot dog stand (a true Icelandic institution, ~600 ISK per dog)
meals.dinner: Fiskmarkaðurinn (The Fish Market) — upscale Icelandic seafood in Reykjavik for a special farewell meal (~8,000–12,000 ISK) or Noodle Station for budget-friendly beef noodle soup (~2,000 ISK)

day_by_day.notes: If your departure flight is very early on Day 13, consider booking an airport hotel near Keflavík for the last night (e.g., Hótel Keflavík or Icelandair Hotel Keflavík) to avoid a stressful early morning drive. Confirm rental car return procedures and fuel requirements.

day_by_day.morning: Final morning — transfer to Keflavík International Airport. Allow at least 2.5–3 hours before departure for check-in, security, and duty-free shopping. Keflavík duty-free is excellent for last-minute Icelandic spirits (Brennivín), chocolates, and cosmetics at good prices.
day_by_day.afternoon: Departure. Reflect on 13 extraordinary days of geothermal hot springs, volcanic landscapes, northern lights, and Icelandic culture.
day_by_day.evening: In-flight or at destination.

meals.breakfast: Airport café or hotel breakfast before transfer — Keflavík Airport has several good breakfast options including Icelandic yogurt and pastries (~1,500–2,500 ISK)
meals.lunch: Airport restaurant or grab snacks for the flight
meals.dinner: In-flight meal

day_by_day.notes: Purchase any remaining Icelandic items at the duty-free store after passport control — it is one of the best-stocked airport duty-free stores in Europe. Confirm your rental car has a full tank before return. Keep your warm layers accessible until you board — Keflavík can be extremely windy and cold.

highlights: Mix of paid and free experiences

trip_options.title: Premium Iceland Escape
trip_options.description: Indulge in the best the destination has to offer. Premium flights, luxury hotels, and exclusive experiences.

hotel.name: Golden Circle & Þingvellir National Park, Southwest Iceland Boutique Stay
hotel.location: Golden Circle & Þingvellir National Park, Southwest Iceland

experiences.name: Northern Lights Hunt by Super Jeep
experiences.description: Join a guided super jeep tour into the Icelandic wilderness away from city light pollution for the best chance of witnessing the Aurora Borealis. Expert guides track solar activity and cloud cover in real time to maximize your viewing experience. Includes hot chocolate and photography tips.
experiences.location: Golden Circle & Þingvellir National Park, Southwest Iceland

experiences.name: Blue Lagoon Geothermal Spa
experiences.description: Soak in the world-famous milky-blue geothermal waters rich in silica and minerals. Enjoy in-water massages, silica mud masks, and a swim-up bar. Booking the evening session dramatically increases your chances of seeing the northern lights dancing above while you relax in the warm 38°C waters.

experiences.name: Secret Lagoon (Gamla Laugin) Soak
experiences.description: Experience Iceland's oldest swimming pool, a natural hot spring dating back to 1891 surrounded by geysers and steaming vents. Far less crowded than the Blue Lagoon, this authentic geothermal pool sits in a stunning rural landscape and offers a genuinely local bathing experience at a fraction of the cost.

experiences.name: Reykjavik Food & Culture Walking Tour
experiences.description: Explore Iceland's vibrant capital through its food scene and Viking heritage. Sample traditional Skyr, lamb soup (Kjötsúpa), fermented shark (Hákarl), and fresh langoustine at local markets and restaurants. Visit the iconic Hallgrímskirkja church, the colorful old harbor, and learn about Norse mythology and Icelandic sagas from a local guide.

experiences.name: Landmannalaugar Highland Hot Springs Hike
experiences.description: Trek through Iceland's dramatic multicolored rhyolite mountains in the Highlands and reward yourself with a natural geothermal hot spring soak at the end. The surreal landscape of obsidian lava fields, steaming fumaroles, and rainbow-colored mountains makes this one of Iceland's most unique and unforgettable experiences.

day_by_day.morning: Arrival at Keflavík International Airport at 13:00 — no morning activities scheduled. Private luxury transfer arranged from airport.
day_by_day.afternoon: After landing, clear customs and meet your private chauffeur. En route to your boutique stay in the Golden Circle area, make a scenic stop at the iconic Öxará River viewpoint near Þingvellir National Park for a brief orientation walk along the rift valley where the North American and Eurasian tectonic plates meet. Arrive at your accommodation, check in, and settle into your luxury suite.
day_by_day.evening: Northern Lights Hunt by Super Jeep — your first evening in Iceland is perfectly timed for a guided super jeep excursion into the dark wilderness away from light pollution. Expert guides will monitor aurora forecasts in real time, driving to optimal viewing locations across the Reykjanes and Golden Circle region. Hot cocoa and warm blankets provided on board.

meals.breakfast: Enjoy a meal on board your flight or at Keflavík Airport's premium lounge before departure.
meals.lunch: Light arrival snack box prepared by your accommodation and waiting in your suite upon check-in — Icelandic cheeses, smoked lamb, skyr parfait, and fresh rye bread.
meals.dinner: Dinner at Lindin Restaurant in Laugarvatn — an intimate fine-dining gem in the Golden Circle area renowned for its locally sourced Arctic char, reindeer tenderloin, and creative New Nordic tasting menus paired with Icelandic craft beers and wines.

day_by_day.notes: January means very limited daylight (roughly 5–6 hours). Aurora activity is weather-dependent; your super jeep guide will adapt routes dynamically. Pack your warmest layers — temperatures can drop to -10°C or lower. Confirm your super jeep tour booking 24 hours in advance.

day_by_day.morning: Explore Þingvellir National Park at dawn — a UNESCO World Heritage Site and the birthplace of the world's oldest parliament (the Alþingi, established 930 AD). Walk the dramatic Almannagjá rift gorge between the tectonic plates, admire the frozen Þingvallavatn Lake (Iceland's largest natural lake), and visit the historic Law Rock (Lögberg). A private guide will provide in-depth historical and geological context.
day_by_day.afternoon: Drive to the legendary Geysir Geothermal Area to witness Strokkur geyser erupting every 5–10 minutes shooting boiling water up to 40 meters high. Continue to the majestic Gullfoss Waterfall — Iceland's most iconic cascade — and walk the viewing platforms as mist freezes into ice crystals in the winter air. A truly cinematic Golden Circle experience.
day_by_day.evening: Return to your boutique accommodation for a private in-suite Nordic spa experience — many luxury properties in this area offer private hot tub access overlooking the dark volcanic landscape. Ideal conditions for a second aurora watch from your own terrace if skies are clear.

meals.breakfast: Full Icelandic breakfast at your boutique hotel — freshly baked rye bread, smoked salmon, skyr with Icelandic honey, free-range eggs, and strong Icelandic coffee.
meals.lunch: Lunch at Hotel Geysir's restaurant — hearty lamb soup, fresh-baked bread, and Icelandic fish of the day, perfectly positioned between Geysir and Gullfoss.
meals.dinner: Private chef dinner arranged at your boutique stay — a curated four-course New Nordic menu featuring Icelandic lamb, wild-caught salmon, foraged herbs, and a decadent skyr cheesecake dessert.

day_by_day.notes: Gullfoss can be icy and slippery in January — wear micro-spike boot attachments (often provided by guides or available at the visitor center). Sunrise is around 11:00 and sunset around 15:30 in mid-January, so plan outdoor photography during this narrow golden-hour window.

day_by_day.morning: Visit the Secret Lagoon (Gamla Laugin) in Flúðir — Iceland's oldest natural swimming pool dating back to 1891. Soak in the geothermally heated waters surrounded by geysers and steam vents in an authentic, non-commercialized setting. The winter atmosphere with snow-dusted surroundings makes this experience particularly magical. Arrive early for a more intimate experience before day-visitors arrive.
day_by_day.afternoon: Explore the charming village of Flúðir and its surrounding greenhouse farms — Iceland's mushroom and tomato cultivation capital, powered entirely by geothermal energy. Arrange a private guided tour of a geothermal greenhouse to understand Iceland's sustainable food production. Afterward, drive through the scenic Haukadalur valley.
day_by_day.evening: Northern Lights Hunt by Super Jeep — a second dedicated aurora hunting expedition departing from the Golden Circle area, venturing further into the highlands for darker skies. Your expert guide will use professional photography equipment to help you capture the lights. Champagne toast under the aurora.

meals.breakfast: Leisurely breakfast at your boutique hotel — Icelandic pancakes (pönnukökur) with bilberry jam, smoked trout, and freshly squeezed Arctic berry juice.
meals.lunch: Lunch at Friðheimar Greenhouse Restaurant in Reykholt — an extraordinary dining experience inside a working tomato greenhouse. Their signature tomato soup and fresh-baked bread are world-famous; book well in advance.
meals.dinner: Dinner at your accommodation or a private catered meal — slow-roasted Icelandic lamb shank with root vegetables, creamy skyr sauce, and a selection of Icelandic craft spirits.

day_by_day.notes: The Secret Lagoon is open year-round and is far less crowded than the Blue Lagoon. Bring your own premium swimwear and a microfiber towel, or use the facilities provided. Water temperature is consistently around 38–40°C. Book Friðheimar lunch reservation well in advance as it fills up quickly even in winter.

day_by_day.morning: Scenic morning drive through the Þingvellir National Park lakeshore — explore the lesser-visited Nesjavellir geothermal power station area with stunning steam plumes rising against the winter sky. Optional snowshoe walk along the lakeshore with a private naturalist guide explaining Iceland's unique geology and birdlife (wintering birds including harlequin ducks frequent the area).
day_by_day.afternoon: Head toward the Kerið Volcanic Crater — a vivid 3,000-year-old caldera with a striking turquoise lake at its base. Walk the entire rim for panoramic views. Continue to the Reykjadalur Valley for a scenic winter hike to the natural hot river where you can bathe in geothermally heated flowing water outdoors amid a snow-covered valley.
day_by_day.evening: Relaxed evening at your boutique accommodation. Private stargazing session on the hotel terrace with a telescope and an expert astronomer guide — January skies in Iceland offer extraordinary views of the Milky Way, Orion, and if lucky, the aurora borealis dancing above.

meals.breakfast: Continental and hot Icelandic breakfast spread at the hotel — skyr bowls, smoked lamb, fresh pastries, and Icelandic herbal teas.
meals.lunch: Packed luxury picnic hamper from your hotel — artisan sandwiches with smoked salmon and cream cheese, thermos of lamb broth, Icelandic chocolate, and hot coffee for the outdoor adventure.
meals.dinner: Dinner at ION Adventure Hotel's LAVA Restaurant (short drive from your accommodation) — a dramatic dining room with panoramic views of the lava fields and Þingvellir. Known for their innovative tasting menus using exclusively Icelandic ingredients.

day_by_day.notes: The Reykjadalur hot river hike is approximately 3km each way and can be muddy and slippery in winter — waterproof hiking boots are essential. Changing facilities at the trailhead are basic; wear your swimsuit under your hiking clothes. The ION LAVA Restaurant reservation is highly recommended well in advance.

day_by_day.morning: Full-day excursion to Reykjavík — private luxury transfer to Iceland's vibrant capital (approximately 45 minutes from the Golden Circle area). Begin with the Reykjavik Food & Culture Walking Tour: explore the historic Old Harbour, the colorful Grandi district, Hallgrímskirkja church, and the Harpa Concert Hall. Sample traditional Skyr, hákarl (fermented shark), Icelandic hot dogs, craft beer, and fresh pastries at artisan markets and local institutions.
day_by_day.afternoon: Continue the Reykjavík culture immersion — visit the National Museum of Iceland for a deep dive into Viking and Norse heritage, then explore the Laugavegur shopping street for premium Icelandic wool sweaters (lopapeysa), design goods, and luxury souvenirs. Visit the Saga Museum for an immersive Viking history experience.
day_by_day.evening: Fine dining evening in Reykjavík before your private transfer back to the Golden Circle accommodation.

meals.breakfast: Early breakfast at your boutique hotel before departure to Reykjavík.
meals.lunch: Included as part of the Reykjavík Food & Culture Walking Tour — multiple tastings across the city's top food spots including Sandholt Bakery, Messinn fish restaurant, and Valdís ice cream.
meals.dinner: Dinner at Dill Restaurant in Reykjavík — Iceland's only Michelin-starred restaurant, offering an extraordinary Nordic tasting menu with wine pairings. Chef Gunnar Karl Gíslason's seasonal creations celebrate Icelandic terroir at the highest level. Essential advance reservation.

day_by_day.notes: Dill Restaurant requires reservations months in advance — ensure this is booked before your trip. The food walking tour typically runs 3–4 hours; wear comfortable walking shoes. Reykjavík's compact size makes it very walkable. Private transfer back to Golden Circle accommodation departs after dinner.

day_by_day.morning: Visit the Haukadalur Geothermal Valley at dawn for a private, crowd-free experience of the Geysir area — your guide will explain the geothermal science and geology in detail. Afterward, explore the nearby Bruarfoss Waterfall — the 'Blue Falls' — a hidden gem with vivid electric-blue cascading waters, accessible via a scenic 2km winter hike.
day_by_day.afternoon: Drive to the Langjökull Glacier (Iceland's second-largest ice cap) for an exclusive glacier experience — snowmobile tour across the vast white expanse or a private ice cave tunnel tour inside the glacier itself. The man-made tunnel system inside Langjökull offers a surreal walk through blue ice corridors.
day_by_day.evening: Return to your boutique accommodation for a restorative evening soak in the private outdoor hot tub. If aurora conditions are favorable, tonight is an excellent opportunity for personal aurora viewing from your property's terrace with zero light pollution.

meals.breakfast: Full hot breakfast at the hotel — eggs cooked to order, Icelandic sausages, smoked fish, fresh-baked bread, and seasonal berry compotes.
meals.lunch: Lunch at Húsafell Resort near Langjökull — a remote luxury lodge serving hearty Icelandic fare including lamb stew, fresh-baked kleinur doughnuts, and hot chocolate to warm up after glacier activities.
meals.dinner: Dinner at your boutique accommodation — chef-prepared three-course meal featuring pan-seared Arctic char with dill butter, roasted root vegetables, and a warm chocolate lava cake with skyr ice cream.

day_by_day.notes: The Langjökull glacier tour requires advance booking through specialized operators (e.g., Into the Glacier). Dress in extreme cold-weather layers — temperatures on the glacier can feel significantly colder than at sea level. The Bruarfoss hike trail may be icy; microspikes recommended.

day_by_day.morning: Dedicated photography morning — with a private professional photographer guide, revisit the most photogenic locations around Þingvellir and the Golden Circle during the brief but spectacular winter golden hour (approximately 11:00–15:30). Capture the dramatic rift valley, frozen lake reflections, and steaming geothermal vents in perfect light conditions.
day_by_day.afternoon: Visit the Laugarvatn Fontana Geothermal Baths — a premium spa facility built directly on the shores of Lake Laugarvatn above natural hot springs. Enjoy steam baths, geothermal pools at varying temperatures, and a unique 'baking bread in the ground' demonstration where rye bread is baked in the geothermal earth and served warm with Icelandic butter.
day_by_day.evening: Northern Lights Hunt by Super Jeep — third dedicated aurora expedition. January statistics show high aurora probability; your expert guide will take you to a new location tonight, potentially toward the Hekla volcano region for a dramatic dark-sky backdrop.

meals.breakfast: Leisurely late breakfast at the hotel — smoked salmon eggs Benedict, freshly squeezed cloudberry juice, and Icelandic flatbread with butter.
meals.lunch: Lunch at Laugarvatn Fontana's café — freshly baked geothermal rye bread with smoked lamb and butter, Icelandic fish soup, and homemade pastries.
meals.dinner: Dinner at Lindin Restaurant in Laugarvatn (return visit for their seasonal winter menu) — a five-course tasting menu with wine pairing, featuring the finest local and foraged Icelandic ingredients.

day_by_day.notes: The private photography session should be pre-arranged with a local professional guide who knows the best winter compositions. Laugarvatn Fontana is a premium facility with changing rooms, towel service, and a quality café — a more refined geothermal experience than many tourist spots.

day_by_day.morning: Day trip toward the South Coast — depart early for the dramatic black sand beaches of Reynisfjara near Vík. Marvel at the towering basalt column formations (Reynisdrangar sea stacks), the powerful Atlantic surf, and the jet-black volcanic beach. A private guide will explain the geological history and Norse mythology associated with the landscape.
day_by_day.afternoon: Continue to Skógafoss Waterfall — one of Iceland's largest and most dramatic waterfalls. In winter, the surrounding rocks and vegetation are often encrusted with ice and frost, creating a fairytale scene. Climb the staircase to the top for panoramic views over the South Coast. Visit the nearby Skógar Folk Museum for insight into traditional Icelandic rural life.
day_by_day.evening: Return to your Golden Circle accommodation. Relaxing evening with a private in-room treatment — arrange a traditional Icelandic hot stone massage with your hotel's spa service, using volcanic basalt stones and Arctic herb-infused oils.

meals.breakfast: Early breakfast at the hotel — packed to-go option of smoked lamb sandwiches, skyr cups, and thermos coffee for the early departure.
meals.lunch: Lunch at Skál! Restaurant in Vík or a premium packed picnic hamper near Skógafoss — Icelandic lamb burger, fish and chips with Arctic herbs, and warm berry soup.
meals.dinner: Dinner at your accommodation — a celebratory mid-trip meal with a premium Icelandic charcuterie board, pan-roasted cod with herb crust, and a selection of Icelandic craft gins and tonics.

day_by_day.notes: Reynisfjara beach is extremely dangerous due to sneaker waves — never turn your back on the ocean and stay behind the safety markers. The drive from Golden Circle to Vík is approximately 2 hours each way; an early start is essential to maximize daylight. South Coast roads can be icy — private driver recommended.

day_by_day.morning: Explore the Kerlingarfjöll Mountain Range — a remote highland destination accessible by super jeep in winter, featuring spectacular geothermal activity, steaming fumaroles, and multicolored rhyolite mountains. This is an off-the-beaten-path alternative to the more commercial sites, offering a raw and dramatic Icelandic landscape experience.
day_by_day.afternoon: Landmannalaugar Highland Hot Springs Hike — trek through Iceland's extraordinary multicolored rhyolite mountains in the Highlands, passing obsidian lava fields, steaming hot springs, and vibrant mineral-stained slopes. Reward yourself with a long soak in the natural geothermal hot spring pool at Landmannalaugar itself, surrounded by snow-dusted mountains. This is one of Iceland's most unique and remote geothermal bathing experiences.
day_by_day.evening: Return to your accommodation via scenic highland route. Quiet evening in — premium room service dinner, a glass of fine wine, and preparation for the final days of the journey.

meals.breakfast: Full hot breakfast at the hotel — fortifying meal before the highland adventure: porridge with Icelandic honey, scrambled eggs with smoked salmon, and strong coffee.
meals.lunch: Packed luxury highland picnic — thermos of hot lamb broth, artisan rye crackers with smoked trout pâté, energy bars, and hot chocolate.
meals.dinner: In-room premium dining experience — a curated selection of Icelandic cheeses, charcuterie, fresh bread, and a bottle of premium Icelandic malt whisky or fine Burgundy wine.

day_by_day.notes: Landmannalaugar is only accessible by 4WD super jeep in winter — book a specialized highland tour operator. The area is remote with no facilities beyond basic huts; your guide will carry all necessary emergency equipment. Bathing suit and towel essential. Weather conditions in the highlands can change rapidly.

day_by_day.morning: Blue Lagoon Geothermal Spa — the crown jewel of Icelandic luxury spa experiences. Book the exclusive Retreat Spa package at the Blue Lagoon for the ultimate premium experience: private changing suites, in-water silica mud mask treatments, algae mask applications, and access to the secluded Retreat section of the lagoon away from general visitors. The milky-blue 38–40°C waters rich in silica, algae, and minerals are legendary for their skin-rejuvenating properties.
day_by_day.afternoon: Continue your Blue Lagoon experience — enjoy the in-water bar (champagne service available), the lava sauna, and the steam cave. Afterward, indulge in a private massage treatment at the Retreat Spa's treatment rooms, followed by afternoon tea in the Lava Restaurant overlooking the lagoon.
day_by_day.evening: Return to your Golden Circle boutique accommodation for a peaceful final evening in the area. Private stargazing and aurora watch from the hotel terrace with expert astronomer. Toast to the journey with Icelandic craft spirits.

meals.breakfast: Breakfast at the hotel before departure to the Blue Lagoon.
meals.lunch: Lunch at the Blue Lagoon's Lava Restaurant — an architectural masterpiece built into the lava field. Indulge in their premium seafood platter, Icelandic lobster bisque, and freshly baked sourdough.
meals.dinner: Farewell dinner at your boutique accommodation — a special chef's table experience with a six-course tasting menu celebrating the best of Icelandic cuisine, paired with natural wines and Icelandic aquavit.

day_by_day.notes: The Blue Lagoon Retreat Spa requires advance booking — ideally several months before your trip. The Retreat package is significantly more exclusive and expensive than the standard entry but offers an incomparable luxury spa experience. Transfer from Golden Circle area to Blue Lagoon is approximately 45 minutes.

day_by_day.morning: Final exploration of Þingvellir National Park — a contemplative morning walk along the Öxará River gorge, visiting the historic Þingvellir Church and the Drowning Pool (Drekkingarhylur). Reflect on Iceland's extraordinary history and geology in one of the country's most sacred landscapes. Private guide available for a deeper historical narrative.
day_by_day.afternoon: Visit to Eyrarbakki and Stokkseyri villages on the South Coast — two of Iceland's oldest coastal settlements. Explore the charming wooden fishing houses, the Húsið Restaurant (one of Iceland's most renowned seafood establishments), and the Þorpið Ghost Centre for a fun cultural detour. Walk along the dramatic black sand coastline.
day_by_day.evening: Northern Lights Hunt by Super Jeep — final dedicated aurora expedition of the trip. Your guide will take you to a specially selected remote location for the best possible conditions. A bottle of Icelandic sparkling wine awaits if the lights appear.

meals.breakfast: Full Icelandic breakfast at the hotel — a celebratory spread with all the classics: smoked fish, skyr, fresh pastries, eggs, and premium coffee.
meals.lunch: Lunch at Húsið Restaurant in Eyrarbakki — legendary for their Icelandic lobster (langoustine) soup, considered by many to be the finest in the country. A must-visit for any serious food lover in Iceland.
meals.dinner: Dinner at your boutique accommodation — light and elegant meal after the aurora hunt: Icelandic fish stew, fresh bread, and a selection of Icelandic herbal teas and desserts.

day_by_day.notes: Húsið Restaurant in Eyrarbakki is a local institution — their lobster soup is world-famous and portions are generous. Reservations recommended. The evening super jeep tour is your last aurora opportunity; January KP index forecasts should be monitored throughout the day.

day_by_day.morning: Leisurely final morning at your Golden Circle boutique accommodation — enjoy a long, indulgent breakfast, pack your bags, and take a final private soak in the outdoor hot tub overlooking the volcanic landscape. A slow, mindful morning to absorb the extraordinary beauty of your surroundings before departure.
day_by_day.afternoon: Scenic drive back toward Reykjavík with stops at any sites not yet visited — consider the Hveragerði Geothermal Town (a small town literally built on top of geothermal activity, with hot springs bubbling up in backyards and greenhouses), and the Hellisheiði Geothermal Power Plant visitor center for a fascinating insight into Iceland's renewable energy infrastructure.
day_by_day.evening: Final night in Reykjavík — check into a luxury city hotel (e.g., Hotel Borg, Holt, or The Retreat at Blue Lagoon for a grand finale). Explore Reykjavík's vibrant evening scene — the city comes alive after dark with galleries, design shops, and world-class bars.

meals.breakfast: Grand final breakfast at your boutique hotel — a leisurely feast celebrating your last morning in the Golden Circle.
meals.lunch: Lunch at Kaffi Krús in Hveragerði — a cozy local café famous for homemade cakes, fresh soups, and Icelandic waffles with cream and jam.
meals.dinner: Farewell dinner at Grillið Restaurant at Radisson Blu Saga Hotel, Reykjavík — a rooftop fine-dining institution with panoramic city views, exceptional Icelandic lamb and seafood, and an extensive wine cellar.

day_by_day.notes: Check-out time at your Golden Circle boutique accommodation is typically 11:00 — arrange a late check-out if your schedule requires it. Reykjavík luxury hotels book up quickly in winter; ensure your final night accommodation is confirmed well in advance.

day_by_day.morning: Final morning in Reykjavík — visit the iconic Hallgrímskirkja church for panoramic rooftop views over the colorful city and surrounding mountains. Explore the Harpa Concert Hall's stunning geometric glass facade and interior. Browse the Kolaportið Flea Market (open weekends) or the premium design stores along Laugavegur for last-minute Icelandic gifts — lopapeysa wool sweaters, Icelandic sea salt, and premium skincare from the Blue Lagoon range.
day_by_day.afternoon: Private luxury transfer to Keflavík International Airport — allow 45–60 minutes driving time plus airport check-in time. Enjoy the Icelandair Business Lounge at Keflavík Airport for a final taste of Icelandic hospitality before departure. Browse the airport's premium duty-free selection for Icelandic spirits (Brennivín, Eimverk whisky), Icelandic chocolates, and local design goods.
day_by_day.evening: Departure from Keflavík International Airport. Carry with you extraordinary memories of aurora-lit skies, steaming geothermal waters, ancient volcanic landscapes, and the warmth of Icelandic hospitality.

meals.breakfast: Premium breakfast at your Reykjavík luxury hotel — a grand final spread with all Icelandic favorites: smoked salmon, skyr, fresh pastries, eggs, and excellent coffee.
meals.lunch: Lunch at Messinn Restaurant on Lækjargata, Reykjavík — celebrated for their signature cast-iron pan-fried fish of the day with butter and herbs, a perfect final taste of Iceland's extraordinary seafood.
meals.dinner: Airport lounge snacks and refreshments, or an in-flight meal on your departure flight.

day_by_day.notes: Allow ample time for airport check-in and security — Keflavík Airport can be busy even in winter. Duty-free shopping at Keflavík is excellent and competitively priced. Consider purchasing Icelandic spirits, Brennivín (Black Death schnapps), and premium Icelandic skincare as premium souvenirs. Ensure all aurora photographs are backed up before departure!
